rules.title: Berkeley ban on coordinated pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use coordinated pricing algorithms (using nonpublic competitor data less than 90 days old) to set rents or occupancy, and no one may sell or license them to Berkeley landlords. Each unit-month is a separate violation, with civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation and a private right of action.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation per unit per month
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential landlords in Berkeley, and algorithm vendors.
rules.exemptions: Aggregated or anonymized reports that do not recommend rents; affordable-housing rent tools; market research for financing or appraisal.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where the landlord uses a covered algorithm.

rules.quoted_span: It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described
rules.conflict_note: Passed to print 2025-11-18 and adopted 2025-12-02, with no effective date stated. A secondary source gives January 2026. Amends existing BMC ch. 13.63. RealPage v. Berkeley was dismissed with prejudice 2026-01-14.

rules.title: Berkeley tenant screening fee rules
rules.requirement: Owners may not charge existing tenants a non-refundable fee to renew a tenancy, including fees for a roommate's departure or for adding or replacing a roommate. Owners who charge a screening fee must first give a Tenant Screening Fee Rights Statement and disclose the Civ. Code § 1950.6 fee cap.
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners and agents of residential rental property in Berkeley.
rules.quoted_span: An owner of residential rental property (or the owner’s agent) cannot charge a non-refundable fee to any existing tenant for the purpose of renewing a tenancy, in whole or in part, including any fee associated with the departure of a roommate or to request to add or replace a roommate in a pre-existing household.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Ordinance just cause for eviction
rules.requirement: Tenants in fully or partially covered units may be evicted only for a just cause. Nonpayment evictions require arrears of at least one month of HUD Fair Market Rent. No eviction is allowed for refusing to sign a similar new lease. Lease-breach evictions require actual harm. Termination notices must reference the Rent Board and be filed with it within 3 business days. A notice of tenant rights is due within 15 days of the start of tenancy. Owner move-in and Ellis evictions require relocation assistance of $19,413, plus $6,471 for qualifying households (2026), adjusted annually for CPI.
rules.coverage_conditions: All fully and partially covered units, including new construction, single-family homes and condos.
rules.exemptions: Golden Duplexes. Units with a kitchen or bath shared with a resident owner. Owner-occupied ADU properties (tenancies after 2018-11-07). Dormitories and nonprofit cooperatives.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner-occupancy exemptions (Golden Duplex, shared facilities, ADU); dormitory and cooperative status.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance (BMC ch. 13.76); Ellis Implementation Ordinance
rules.quoted_span: In Berkeley, tenants in units that are fully or partially covered by the Rent Ordinance cannot be evicted unless there is "just cause” (previously called “good cause”).
rules.conflict_note: The Measure BB amendments (Nov. 2024) have no stated effective date. The notice of rights applies to tenancies starting on or after 2024-12-20. The 2026 relocation amounts took effect 2026-01-01.

rules.title: Berkeley Rent Stabilization Ordinance rent ceilings and Annual General Adjustment
rules.requirement: Rents on fully covered units may rise only by the Annual General Adjustment: 65% of Bay Area CPI, capped at 5% by Measure BB, and 1.0% for 2026. Eligible landlords must give notice, and banked AGAs remain available. Capital improvement petitions are allowed only for completed work. For tenancies starting on or after 2024-02-06, utilities must be included in base rent unless separately metered in the tenant's name.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units in multifamily properties with a certificate of occupancy on or before June 1980. Single-family homes are covered only for tenancies that began before 1996. Rooming houses are covered.
rules.exemptions: Units with a certificate of occupancy after June 1980. Most condos and post-1995 single-family tenancies (Costa-Hawkins). Certain HUD-insured subsidized units. Golden Duplexes. Units with a kitchen or bath shared with the owner. Owner-occupied ADU properties. Dormitories and cooperatives.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Single-family and condo coverage depends on tenancy start date. Subsidy type. Golden Duplex, shared kitchen/bath and owner-occupied ADU exemptions.

rules.citation: Berkeley Mun. Code ch. 13.76 (§ 13.76.110A); Rent Board Reg. 1148; Measure BB (Nov. 2024)

rules.conflict_note: Sources state the cutoff both as 'built before 1980' and as 'certificate of occupancy after June 1980'. Measure BB (Nov. 2024) amendments have no stated effective date. The 1.0% AGA applies to 2026 only.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not ask about or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection or other decisions. Any adverse action based on criminal history requires written notice and an opportunity to respond. The applicant notice must be posted.
rules.key_value: No criminal history inquiry or use
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing providers in Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied 1-3 unit properties. Lifetime sex offender registrants. Limited public housing and Section 8 exemptions. Owner move-back agreements. Sublets and roommate additions.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner-occupancy exemption for buildings of 3 units or fewer; program-specific exemptions.

rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.
rules.conflict_note: Only the passage date (2020-04-14) is stated.

rules.title: Berkeley security deposit interest
rules.requirement: Landlords of fully or partially covered units must pay interest on security deposits at the end of each year. If the tenant moves out mid-year, a prorated amount is due.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units fully or partially covered by the Berkeley Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Golden Duplexes. Units with a kitchen or bath shared with the owner. Owner-occupied ADU properties. Dormitories and cooperatives.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Owner-occupancy exemptions.

rules.citation: Berkeley Rent Stabilization and Eviction for Good Cause Ordinance (security deposit interest)
rules.quoted_span: For tenancies in units fully or partially covered by Berkeley's Rent Ordinance, landlords must pay tenants interest on their security deposit at the end of each year and a prorated amount if the tenant moves out before the end of the year.
rules.conflict_note: The rate and code section are not stated.

rules.title: Boston tenant eviction protections home rule petition (H.3744)
rules.requirement: A home rule petition to authorize eviction protections in Boston was not enacted. It imposes no just-cause requirement.

rules.title: Boston Housing Stability Notification Act
rules.requirement: Landlords ending a tenancy must give the Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources together with the notice to quit or non-renewal, and must submit a copy of the notice to the City through its portal. Penalty is a warning, then $300 per day.
rules.coverage_conditions: All Boston landlords and foreclosing owners ending tenancies.
rules.exemptions: Hospital, nursing and health facilities; short-term substance abuse treatment facilities.

rules.requirement: A home rule petition to authorize rent stabilization in Boston was sent to a study order and not enacted. It imposes no cap.
rules.coverage_conditions: Boston residential rentals (proposed).
rules.quoted_span: By Representative Montaño of Boston, a petition (accompanied by bill, House, No. 3744) of Samantha Montaño (with the approval of the mayor and city council) that the city of Boston be authorized to implement rent stabilization and tenant eviction protections.
rules.conflict_note: G.L. c. 40P bars local rent control.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.requirement: Covered providers may not use blanket criminal bans, non-conviction arrests, sealed or juvenile records, or convictions older than 5 years. They may not use credit scores; credit history may be used only in lieu of rental history.
rules.coverage_conditions: DND-funded or DND-land providers; IDP income-restricted units.
rules.exemptions: Direct-relationship and risk-of-harm exceptions; federal or state requirements.

rules.title: Boston fair housing ban including rental assistance
rules.requirement: Housing discrimination is barred in Boston, including on the basis of receipt of rental assistance such as Section 8.
rules.coverage_conditions: All Boston housing rentals.
rules.citation: Boston fair housing ordinance (Boston Fair Housing Commission)
rules.quoted_span: In the City of Boston, it’s illegal to discriminate when renting, buying, selling, or securing financing for any housing.
rules.conflict_note: No ordinance citation is given.

rules.title: AB 325 Cartwright Act ban on common pricing algorithms
rules.requirement: No person may use or distribute a common pricing algorithm (one used by two or more persons that uses competitor data) as part of a contract, combination or conspiracy to restrain trade. No person may use or distribute such an algorithm while coercing another person to adopt its recommended price or terms.
rules.coverage_conditions: Any person, including landlords and rental software vendors. This is general antitrust law, not specific to housing.
rules.exemptions: End consumers; single-firm algorithms that use only the firm's own data.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a common pricing algorithm is used in a conspiracy or with coercion.

rules.citation: Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 16729 (AB 325, Stats. 2025, ch. 338)
rules.quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date inferred from the default rule for regular-session statutes (chaptered 2025-10-06).

rules.title: California application screening fee cap and handling requirements
rules.requirement: Screening fees are limited to actual out-of-pocket cost, and never more than $30 per applicant adjusted for CPI since 1998 ($68.96 in 2026). No fee may be charged when no unit is available. A fee may be charged only under a first-qualified-applicant process or with a full refund to non-selected applicants. Landlords must give an itemized receipt and a copy of the credit report within 7 days, and must refund unused portions.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords and agents charging residential rental applicants, including guarantors.
rules.exemptions: Does not preempt housing assistance program fee rules.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant.
rules.conflict_note: The original effective date is not stated. The latest amendment (AB 1170) took effect 2026-01-01. The 2026 dollar figure comes from the Berkeley Rent Board.

rules.title: Tenant Protection Act statewide just cause eviction requirement
rules.requirement: After a tenant has occupied the unit lawfully for 12 months (or 24 months for one tenant if adult tenants were added), the owner may terminate only for an enumerated at-fault or no-fault just cause, stated in the written notice. Curable violations require a notice to cure. For no-fault terminations the owner must either pay one month's rent as relocation assistance within 15 days or waive the final month's rent. Owners must also give tenants the statutory notice of rent cap and just cause protections in at least 12-point type. A noncompliant termination notice is void.
rules.key_value: Just cause after 12 months; 1 month's rent relocation for no-fault
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property in California, including mobilehome park units, after 12 months of tenancy, unless displaced by a qualifying local just cause ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Units with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years. Transient hotels, care facilities and dormitories. Tenants sharing a bath or kitchen with a resident owner. Owner-occupied single-family homes renting no more than two units or bedrooms. Owner-occupied duplexes. Non-corporate separately alienable units, if notice was given. Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: 12-month occupancy requirement. Non-corporate single-family/condo exemption requires notice. Owner-occupancy and shared-facility exemptions. Deed-restricted affordable housing excluded.

rules.interaction: Yields to a stricter local rule in the same category where one covers the unit.
rules.quoted_span: (a) Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.
rules.conflict_note: The current text has been operative since 2024-04-01 and was amended by AB 1529 effective 2026-01-01. It is repealed 2030-01-01. The original Tenant Protection Act just cause rules date from 2020.

rules.title: Housing Crisis Act relocation for lower-income households displaced by demolition
rules.requirement: Lower-income households displaced when protected units are demolished for new construction must receive relocation benefits equal to those public entities pay under Gov. Code § 7260 et seq.
rules.coverage_conditions: Lower-income (80% AMI or below) households in protected units demolished for new housing development.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: RESTRICTED: lower-income households in protected units demolished for new construction.

rules.citation: Cal. Gov. Code § 66300.6(b)(4)(A) (SB 330, as amended by SB 8 and AB 1218)

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act (AB 1482) statewide rent increase cap
rules.requirement: Owners may not raise gross rent over any 12-month period by more than 5% plus the regional CPI change, or 10%, whichever is lower. The increase is measured from the lowest rent charged in the prior 12 months, and no more than two increases are allowed in a 12-month period. Rent may be reset on a new tenancy where no prior tenant remains. State law also requires 30 days' written notice for increases under 10%.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property statewide, including mobilehome park units, unless covered by stricter local rent control or another exemption.
rules.exemptions: Units with a certificate of occupancy issued within the previous 15 years (rolling). Deed-restricted or subsidized affordable housing. Dormitories. Units under stricter local rent control. Separately alienable single-family homes and condos not owned by a REIT, corporation or LLC with a corporate member, if the exemption notice was given. Owner-occupied duplexes. Mobilehome homeowners.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Single-family/condo exemption requires a non-corporate owner and a written exemption notice. Owner-occupied duplex exemption. Deed-restricted/subsidized affordable housing and dormitories are excluded.

rules.interaction: Yields to a stricter local rule in the same category where one covers the unit.
rules.quoted_span: Subject to subdivision (b), an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.
rules.conflict_note: Original AB 1482 took effect 2020-01-01 and the cap applies to increases on or after 2019-03-15. The current text (SB 567, Stats. 2023 ch. 290) has been operative since 2024-04-01. The section is repealed 2030-01-01. The 30-day notice rule comes from an LAHD summary that cites no statute.

rules.title: FEHA ban on source-of-income discrimination, including Section 8 and subsidy screening rules
rules.requirement: Owners may not discriminate based on source of income, which includes housing subsidies such as Section 8 and VASH; 'No Section 8' policies are barred. For subsidized applicants, income standards must be based only on the tenant's portion of the rent. Credit history may be used only if the applicant is offered the option of alternative evidence of ability to pay. Income standards must count the aggregate income of co-residents.
rules.coverage_conditions: Owners of housing accommodations in California.
rules.exemptions: An owner-occupant renting to one additional person.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Subsidy-specific screening limits apply only to applicants with a government rent subsidy.

rules.quoted_span: (a) For the owner of any housing accommodation to discriminate against or harass any person because of the race, color, religion, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, national origin, ancestry, familial status, source of income, disability, veteran or military status, or genetic information of that person.
rules.conflict_note: SB 329 extended source-of-income protection to subsidies effective 2020-01-01. The SB 267 credit-history provisions (current text) took effect 2024-01-01.

rules.title: FEHA / Civil Rights Council limits on criminal history screening
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not impose blanket bans on people with criminal histories. They may not consider arrests that did not lead to conviction, or sealed, expunged or juvenile records. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to tenancy and safety, considering its nature and severity.
rules.key_value: No blanket bans; no arrests without conviction
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing providers and tenant screening companies in California.
rules.exemptions: An owner-occupant renting to one additional person.
rules.citation: California Civil Rights Council criminal history housing regulations under FEHA
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.
rules.conflict_note: The regulation section numbers are not given in the sources.

rules.title: California security deposit cap and handling rules
rules.requirement: Security deposits may not exceed one month's rent, in addition to first month's rent. Qualifying small landlords may collect two months' rent, but not from service members. Deposits may not be labeled nonrefundable. Deductions are limited to unpaid rent, damage beyond ordinary wear and tear, and cleaning to move-in condition. Landlords must offer a pre-move-out inspection. Photos are required at move-out (from 2025-04-01) and at move-in (for tenancies starting on or after 2025-07-01). The deposit must be returned within 21 days with an itemized statement, receipts and proof of repairs, and returned electronically if it was paid electronically (from 2026-01-01). Bad-faith retention exposes the landlord to up to 2x the deposit in damages.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent (2 months for qualifying small landlords); return within 21 days
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental agreements in California. The cap applies to security collected or demanded on or after 2024-07-01.
rules.exemptions: Small landlords (natural persons or LLCs of natural persons owning no more than 2 rental properties with no more than 4 units total) may collect 2 months' rent, except from service members.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Higher two-month cap depends on owner form and total portfolio.

rules.quoted_span: (c) (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.
rules.conflict_note: 2024-07-01 is the date of the one-month cap (AB 12). Photo, proof-of-repair and electronic-return provisions took effect 2025-01-01, 2025-04-01, 2025-07-01 and 2026-01-01.

rules.title: Cambridge Tenants Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO just cause eviction and relocation assistance
rules.requirement: RSO tenants may be evicted only for enumerated at-fault or no-fault reasons. Nonpayment evictions require arrears above one month's Fair Market Rent (since 2023-03-27). No-fault evictions require a Declaration of Intent to Evict filed with LAHD before service, and termination notices must be filed with LAHD within 3 business days. No-fault evictions also require relocation assistance made available within 15 days. For 7/1/2026-6/30/2027 the amounts are: eligible tenants $11,000 or $14,400; qualified tenants $23,150 or $27,400; reduced Mom & Pop amounts for owner/family move-ins.

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (non-RSO units)

Landlords must give the Notice of Renters' Protections (tenancies from 2023-01-27) and must post and provide the Notice of Right to Counsel (from 2025-08-20).

rules.title: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance allowable rent increase
rules.requirement: Rent on RSO units may rise once every 12 months by the LAHD allowable percentage, which was 3% for 2025-07-01 through 2026-06-30. From 2026-02-02, no utility add-on and no 10% increase for an added dependent are allowed; 10% is still allowed for an added non-dependent tenant. RSO and SCEP fee pass-throughs ($1.61 and $2.83 per month) are allowed with registration and notice. Rent resets on voluntary vacancy.

rules.title: Los Angeles RSO security deposit interest

rules.quoted_span: An Act prohibiting algorithmic rent setting
rules.conflict_note: Reported favorably 2026-03-12 and sent to Senate Ways and Means.

rules.title: Massachusetts limit on upfront charges (no application fees)
rules.requirement: At or before the start of a tenancy, a lessor or its agent may require only first month's rent, last month's rent, a security deposit and the cost of a lock and key. Application and other fees are barred.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential tenancies.
rules.exemptions: Vacation tenancies of 100 days or less.
rules.quoted_span: (b) At or prior to the commencement of any tenancy, no lessor or agent of the lessor may require a tenant or prospective tenant to pay, to the lessor or to an agent of the lessor, any amount in excess of the following:
rules.conflict_note: In force since the 1970s. Extended to lessor's agents effective 2025-08-01 (St. 2025, c. 9).

rules.title: Massachusetts broker fee paid by hiring party
rules.requirement: A broker fee may be paid only by the party who engaged the broker. Brokers must disclose fee terms in writing.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rentals involving licensed brokers.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a broker is involved.

rules.quoted_span: Any fee shall only be paid by the party, lessor or tenant who originally engaged and entered into a contract with the licensed broker or salesperson.

rules.title: Massachusetts notice-to-quit requirements
rules.requirement: Tenancies at will end only on a notice equal to the rent period or 30 days (whichever is longer). Nonpayment requires a 14-day notice, with a right to cure (10 days for at-will tenants once per 12 months; by the answer date for lease tenants) and a mandatory state form. Courts must grant a continuance for government payment delays. There is no just-cause requirement.
rules.coverage_conditions: Massachusetts residential tenancies.
rules.quoted_span: Section 12. Estates at will may be determined by either party by three months' notice in writing for that purpose given to the other party; and, if the rent reserved is payable at periods of less than three months, the time of such notice shall be sufficient if it is equal to the interval between the days of payment or thirty days, whichever is longer.
rules.conflict_note: This is a procedure rule, not just cause.

rules.title: Massachusetts anti-retaliation
rules.requirement: Reprisals against tenants for protected activity are barred. A termination notice (other than for nonpayment) or a rent increase within 6 months of such activity is presumed retaliatory. Damages are 1-3 months' rent or actual damages.
rules.coverage_conditions: Massachusetts residential tenants.
rules.exemptions: Nonpayment terminations.
rules.quoted_span: The receipt of any notice of termination of tenancy, except for nonpayment of rent, or, of increase in rent, or, of any substantial alteration in the terms of tenancy within six months after the tenant has commenced, proceeded with, or obtained relief in such action, exercised such rights, made such report or complaint, or organized or joined such tenants' union or within six months after any other person has taken such action or actions on behalf of the tenant or in, or relating to, the building in which the tenant resides, shall create a rebuttable presumption that such notice or other action is a reprisal against the tenant for engaging in such activities.

rules.title: Massachusetts statewide rent control initiative (IP 25-21), struck by SJC
rules.requirement: Would have repealed G.L. c. 40P and capped increases at the lesser of CPI or 5%. The SJC barred it from the November 2026 ballot, so it is not law.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential units statewide, as proposed.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied buildings of 4 units or fewer; units under 10 years old; and others.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Never took effect.

rules.citation: Initiative Petition 25-21; Cella v. Attorney General, SJC-13893 (2026)
rules.quoted_span: Under the proposed law, annual rent increases would have been limited to the lesser of the annual increase in the Consumer Price Index or 5%.
rules.conflict_note: Struck 2026-06-23. G.L. c. 40P § 4 continues to bar local rent control.

rules.title: M.G.L. c. 151B § 4 housing discrimination and source of income
rules.requirement: Landlords may not discriminate against recipients of public assistance or housing subsidies, may not make inquiries about protected characteristics, and may not refuse to rent because children will occupy the unit.
rules.coverage_conditions: Persons furnishing rental accommodations in Massachusetts.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two-family units (subsections 7 and 11); small dwellings with an elderly or infirm occupant (children protection).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The source-of-income subsection (10) has no owner exemption.

rules.quoted_span: 10. For any person furnishing credit, services or rental accommodations to discriminate against any individual who is a recipient of federal, state, or local public assistance, including medical assistance, or who is a tenant receiving federal, state, or local housing subsidies, including rental assistance or rental supplements, because the individual is such a recipient, or because of any requirement of such public assistance, rental assistance, or housing subsidy program.

rules.title: Massachusetts security deposit law
rules.requirement: Deposits are capped at one month's rent. Landlords must give a receipt and a statement of condition within 10 days, and hold the deposit in a separate interest-bearing Massachusetts account with a receipt within 30 days. Interest of 5% (or the bank rate) is due annually. The deposit must be returned within 30 days with only permitted deductions, and transferred to a successor owner with notice within 45 days. Violations carry treble damages. An optional fee in lieu of deposit is allowed by regulation, with the total capped at 1 month.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in Massachusetts.
rules.exemptions: Vacation tenancies of 100 days or less.
rules.quoted_span: (iii) a security deposit equal to the first month's rent provided that such security deposit is deposited as required by subsection (3) and that the tenant is given the statement of condition as required by subsection (2);

rules.title: Newark Rent Control anti-reprisal eviction ban
rules.requirement: Landlords may not seek possession in reprisal for a tenant's efforts to enforce rent control rights.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by Newark rent control.
rules.quoted_span:
Your landlord shall not bring action to recover possession of your apartment as a reprisal of 
your efforts to enforce your rights under Rent Control.
rules.conflict_note: State Anti-Eviction Act protections also apply.

rules.title: Newark Rent Control Ordinance CPI-U cap
rules.requirement: Rent may rise annually only by the published CPI-U percentage, with 30 days' written notice. Larger increases require Board approval. Landlords must register with the Division of Rent Control before raising rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: Newark residential rental dwellings.
rules.exemptions: Public housing, transient hotels and commercial space. New construction exempt for 30 years with a certificate of exemption. Rehabilitation exemptions.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: The 30-year exemption requires a pre-occupancy certificate; rehabilitation exemptions require a Board certificate.

rules.quoted_span:
permissible annual rent increases for a given month are shown in the table  below. Landlords may 
increase rents as per the Consumer Price Index - Urban percentage (CPI-U %) published every 
month.
rules.conflict_note: Enacted 1973-11-20. The CPI-U formula has applied since 2014-06-20 and the ordinance was overhauled 2019-09-11. A COVID freeze ran from 2020-04 to 2023-09.

rules.title: NJ FAIR Act ban on algorithmic rent-setting coordinators
rules.requirement: Rental property owners may not pay for or use a coordinator (algorithmic revenue management software using competitors' nonpublic data). Coordinators may not facilitate anticompetitive agreements or parallel pricing. Violations are violations of the NJ Antitrust Act.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental property owners and coordinators in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions: Government affordability controls, research, free public estimates, brokerage databases and spreadsheets requiring human analysis.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where covered software is used.

rules.conflict_note: Approved 2026-07-20. Section 6(b) bars conflicting municipal ordinances, which may preempt the Jersey City and Hoboken bans once effective.

rules.title: New Jersey $50 rental application fee cap
rules.requirement: Landlords may not charge an application or similar fee above $50. The cap is CPI-adjusted annually from 2027-01-01.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rentals other than one- and two-family dwellings.
rules.exemptions: One- and two-family dwellings; real estate licensees who are not the landlord.
rules.quoted_span:
1. a. A landlord, or
agent thereof, shall not require an application or other similar fee to apply
to lease or sublease a residential rental property for dwelling purposes, which
exceeds $50.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date computed from the fourth month following enactment on 2026-01-20.

rules.title: New Jersey Anti-Eviction Act good cause requirement
rules.requirement: Residential landlords may not evict or refuse to renew a lease without a statutory good cause, and must serve the required notices. Illegal-occupancy evictions require relocation of 6 months' rent. Self-help lockouts are illegal (N.J.S.A. 2A:39-1), and reprisal evictions are barred (2A:42-10.10). Foreclosure is not grounds for eviction, and buyers must notify tenants within 10 business days (2A:50-69). Landlords must distribute the Truth in Renting statement (46:8-43).
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals, including single-family homes, mobile homes and rooming houses.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with no more than two rental units. Transient or seasonal guests. Units held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Transient/seasonal and family-trust exemptions.

rules.quoted_span:
No residential landlord may evict or fail to renew a 
lease, whether it is a written or an oral lease without good cause.

rules.title: Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act (conversions)
rules.requirement: Eligible senior, disabled or disabled-veteran tenants in buildings converted to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership may be protected from eviction for up to 40 years, subject to income limits. Rents may not be raised to cover costs resulting solely from the conversion.
rules.coverage_conditions: Buildings undergoing conversion.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: RESTRICTED: eligible senior/disabled tenants in buildings undergoing condo/co-op conversion.

rules.quoted_span:
Tenants may be protected from eviction for 40 years 
if their family income is not more than three (3) times the average per person income in their 
county or $50,000.00, whichever  is greater (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.28).

rules.title: New Jersey ban on unconscionable rent increases
rules.requirement: There is no statewide numeric rent cap. Increases must not be unconscionable and must comply with municipal rent ordinances. An increase takes effect only after a valid notice to quit and notice of increase.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies covered by the Anti-Eviction Act.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units.
rules.interaction: Yields to a stricter local rule in the same category where one covers the unit.
rules.quoted_span:
The increase in rent must not be 
unconscionable; it must not be so unreasonable as to shock the conscience of a fair and honest 
person and must comply with any municipal ordinances governing rent increases.
rules.conflict_note: New construction is exempt from municipal rent control for 30 years (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5).

rules.title: New Jersey Fair Chance in Housing Act
rules.requirement: Providers may make no criminal record inquiry before a conditional offer. Afterward they may consider only specified convictions within lookback periods, and must make an individualized assessment. Discriminatory advertising is banned, as are drug and alcohol tests of applicants.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental housing providers in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied premises of 4 units or fewer.
rules.quoted_span:
shall not make any oral or written inquiry
regarding an applicant’s criminal record prior to making a conditional offer.
rules.conflict_note: Effective date computed from the seventh month following approval on 2021-06-18.

rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination, including source of lawful income
rules.requirement: Landlords may not refuse to rent or discriminate based on protected classes, including source of lawful income or rent payment such as Section 8.
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlord-tenant relationships in New Jersey.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two-family dwellings; rooms in owner-occupied single-family homes.
rules.quoted_span:
The New Jersey Law Against Discrimination (LAD), 
N.J.S.A. 10:5-12(g) to -(h), prohibits discrimination when selling or renting property and requires 
equal treatment in the sale or rental of housing regardless of race, creed, color, national origin, 
ancestry, sex, marital status, civil union status, domestic partnership status, familial status, 
affectional or sexual orientation, gender  identity or expression, mental and physical disability, 
nationality, or source of lawful income.

rules.title: New Jersey Security Deposit Law
rules.requirement: Deposits may not exceed 1.5 months' rent, and annual increases may not exceed 10%. Deposits must be held in an interest-bearing New Jersey account, and the tenant must be notified within 30 days; interest belongs to the tenant. The deposit plus interest, less itemized deductions, must be returned within 30 days. Wrongful withholding carries double damages.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rentals.
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwellings (unless the tenant opts in). Seasonal rentals of 125 days or less.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Seasonal-rental exemption and tenant opt-in.

rules.quoted_span:
The maximum-security deposit to be collected by the landlord cannot be more than 
one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ).

rules.title: San Diego ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: Landlords may not use algorithmic devices that rely on nonpublic competitor data to set rents or occupancy. Tenants may sue for damages, injunctive relief and penalties up to $1,000 per violation, with each month and property a separate violation.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in San Diego.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a covered device is used.

rules.quoted_span: San Diego similarly authorizes tenant suits for damages, injunctive relief and penalties of up to $1,000 per violation, with each month and affected rental property potentially constituting a separate violation.
rules.conflict_note: Secondary source gives only the month. Draft ordinance materials (O-2025-107) were not used.

rules.title: San Diego Residential Tenant Protections just cause ordinance
rules.requirement: From the start of a tenancy longer than 30 days, landlords may terminate only for enumerated at-fault or no-fault just cause, with a cure notice for curable violations. No-fault terminations require relocation of 2 months' rent (3 months for seniors or disabled tenants) and a 5-year right of first offer. Landlords must give the tenant protections notice and the Tenant Protection Guide. Buyout agreements must exceed the relocation owed. Termination notices must be filed with SDHC within 3 business days once its portal is noticed.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in San Diego, tenancies over 30 days.
rules.exemptions: Units with a certificate of occupancy within the previous 15 years. Deed-restricted affordable housing (Section 8 tenants remain covered). Shared kitchen or bath with the owner. Owner-occupied single-family homes and two-unit properties. Non-corporate separately alienable units with notice. Hotels, care facilities and dormitories.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Non-corporate single-family/condo exemption requires notice; owner-occupancy exemptions; affordable housing excluded.

rules.citation: San Diego Mun. Code ch. 9, art. 8, div. 7 (§ 98.0701 et seq.)
rules.quoted_span:
A landlord shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause. For purposes of this 
Division, just cause includes at-fault just cause and no-fault just cause.
rules.conflict_note: Amended by O-21769 N.S. effective 2024-03-28. The SDHC filing requirement depends on the portal launch, which is unverified.

rules.title: San Francisco ban on algorithmic rent-setting devices
rules.requirement: The sale or use of algorithmic devices that use nonpublic competitor data to set rents or manage occupancy is prohibited. Tenants or the City Attorney may sue for damages, injunctive relief and civil penalties up to $1,000 per violation; each unit-month may be a separate violation.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential units in San Francisco.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a covered device is used.

rules.quoted_span: adding Section 37.10C to the Rent Ordinance went into effect on October 14, 2024. The law prohibits the sale or use of algorithmic devices to set rents or manage occupancy levels for residential units in San Francisco.
rules.conflict_note: Approved by the Board of Supervisors in July 2024.

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance just cause eviction and relocation
rules.requirement: Evictions from covered units require one of 17 just causes, and it must be the landlord's dominant motive; lease expiration or a sale is not cause. Relocation is owed for owner/relative move-in, demolition, capital improvement and rehab evictions (§ 37.9C; notices 3/1/26-2/28/27): $8,245 per tenant, up to $24,733 per unit, plus $5,497 per elderly or disabled tenant or household with children. Ellis evictions (§ 37.9A) owe $11,110.05 per tenant, up to $33,330.13, plus $7,443.90. Temporary displacements under 20 days owe $446 per day plus moving costs under Civ. Code § 1947.9.
rules.coverage_conditions: Units covered by the Rent Ordinance's eviction provisions, including post-1979 units and Costa-Hawkins tenancies.
rules.exemptions: Units not covered by the Rent Ordinance (not listed in the source).

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Exemptions from eviction coverage are not stated.

rules.citation: S.F. Admin. Code §§ 37.9(a), 37.9A, 37.9C; Cal. Civ. Code § 1947.9
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.
rules.conflict_note: Relocation rates adjust each March 1. The relocation archive starts in 2006. Civ. Code § 1947.9 is a state statute applying to SF temporary displacements.

rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance annual allowable increase
rules.requirement: Rents on rent-controlled units may rise only by the annual allowable increase set by the Rent Board: 1.6% of base rent for 2026-03-01 through 2027-02-28.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rent-controlled units under the SF Rent Ordinance.
rules.exemptions: Units first receiving a certificate of occupancy after June 13, 1979. Costa-Hawkins-eligible tenancies. Some units regulated by other agencies.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Costa-Hawkins single-family/condo tenancies are exempt from increase limits.

rules.quoted_span: For rent-controlled units, the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%.
rules.conflict_note: The CO cutoff comes from the SF just-cause page (c184). The rate resets each March 1; prior rates were 1.4% (2025-26) and 1.7% (2024-25).

value_schedule.quoted_span: The annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2025 through February 28, 2026 is 1.4%
the annual allowable increase amount effective March 1, 2026 through February 28, 2027 is 1.6%

rules.title: San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance (affordable housing)
rules.requirement: Limits use of arrest and conviction history in affordable housing decisions in San Francisco.
rules.coverage_conditions: Affordable housing providers in San Francisco.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: RESTRICTED: affordable housing decisions only.

rules.quoted_span: San Francisco's Fair Chance Ordinance protects residents with arrest or conviction history in affordable housing decisions.
rules.conflict_note: Agency summary only; no code citation or date.

rules.title: San Francisco security deposit interest
rules.requirement: Landlords must pay interest on tenant security deposits at the Rent Board rate: 4.2% for 2026-03-01 through 2027-02-28.
rules.coverage_conditions: San Francisco residential tenancies with security deposits.
rules.citation: San Francisco Rent Board Topic No. 572 (Security Deposit Interest Rates)
rules.quoted_span:
Security Deposit Interest:
4.2% for March 1, 2026 – February 28, 2027
rules.conflict_note: The underlying ordinance citation is not given. Prior rates were 5.0% (2025-26) and 5.2% (2024-25).

rules.title: Santa Ana ban on automated rent price-fixing (NS-3090)
rules.requirement: The sale, licensing and use of algorithmic rent-setting software that relies on nonpublic competitor data is prohibited. Tenants may bring private claims for up to $1,000 per violation per month.
rules.key_value: Up to $1,000 per violation per month
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential rental property in Santa Ana, and software sellers.
rules.exemptions: Software using only public or aggregate historical data; affordable-housing compliance tools.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Applies only where a covered tool is used.

rules.quoted_span: Ordinance NS-3090 prohibits specified anticompetitive automated rent price-fixing; private tenant claims and up to $1,000 per violation and per month.
rules.conflict_note: First reading 2026-02-17 and final vote 2026-03-03. A news source says March 2026, but the 30-day rule gives about 2026-04-02.

rules.title: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance
rules.requirement: After 30 days of tenancy, an owner may terminate only for an enumerated just cause stated in a written notice, with a cure notice for curable violations. No-fault terminations require 3 months of relocation assistance or a waiver of the final 3 months' rent. Owners must notify tenants of the protections.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential tenancies in Santa Ana over 30 days.
rules.exemptions: Housing produced in the last 15 years. Deed-restricted affordable housing. Transient occupancy, care facilities, dormitories and shared quarters.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Excludes deed-restricted affordable housing and facility types.

rules.citation: Santa Ana Just Cause Eviction Ordinance (2021)
rules.quoted_span: After 30 days, an owner shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in a written notice.
rules.conflict_note: The source does not say whether the 15-year exemption is measured by construction date or certificate of occupancy.

rules.title: Santa Ana Rent Stabilization Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rent may be raised once a year by no more than the lesser of 3% or 80% of the CPI change, and not at all if CPI is negative. The cap is 2.87% for 9/1/2026-8/31/2027. Owners must give written notice of the ordinance at lease start and with any rent increase. Owners may petition for a fair-return increase.
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential buildings constructed on or before 1995-02-01; mobile home spaces offered for rent on or before 1990-01-01.
rules.exemptions: Buildings constructed after 1995-02-01.

coverage.unverifiable_conditions: Costa-Hawkins may exempt single-family homes and condos.

rules.quoted_span: Increase in residential rents are limited to the lower of 3% per year, or 80% of the percent change in the Consumer Price Index over the most recent 12-month period.

value_schedule.quoted_span: 2.87 percent is the maximum allowable rent increase for the period of September 1, 2026 through August 31, 2027.
